description:
Heap exposes six public collect entry points over one private body (gc, gc_with_extra_root_slots, gc_with_any_value_ref_roots, gc_with_value_and_any_value_ref_roots, gc_process_roots, gc_any_value_roots_with_process_roots), and the three scheduler sites assemble roots differently: exec/runtime.rs and aot_shim.rs root the runnable closure and the mailbox; ir_codegen/compiled.rs additionally roots the park record's clause bodies and after continuation and rewrites them afterwards. Whether a parked process's clause closures are rooted depends on which path collected it.

BEAM has one setup_rootset (erl_gc.c) that gathers every root of a process in one place, and one erts_garbage_collect(p, need, objv, nobj).

Done when:
- Process has one collect method that builds the root set from the process (runnable closure, park record closures and bound values, mailbox, in-queue gifts not yet grafted if any can be live, plus caller-supplied transient roots) and calls one Heap::collect(roots). The six public Heap gc_* functions reduce to that one plus whatever the heap tests need, and anything kept only for tests moves behind cfg(test).
- exec/runtime.rs, aot_shim.rs and ir_codegen/compiled.rs (and the interpreter's back-edge path in ir_interp/backend.rs if it collects) call the one method. No site assembles roots itself.
- A test parks a process on a receive whose clause bodies and bound values live on its heap, forces a collection through each of the three paths, and shows the park record's closures forwarded and still callable (the receive still matches after the collection).
- The fixture matrix for 00694 to 00698 is unchanged, and the fz.runtime.gc root_heap_edges pins are reported before and after; a change in root count is explained in the commit or is a stop.
- Full gate green. Commit in Why / What changed / Verification form. No co-author trailer.

Tests: the three-path park-and-collect test above (one test per path, same program), and a test that a mailbox value and a runnable closure are both forwarded by the single entry.
title: One root set, one collect entry, shared by JIT, AOT and interpreter
